headline: The Senate voted down S. 3436, which would have required the President to impose sanctions tied to the Nord Stream 2 natural gas pipeline.
what_it_does: If adopted, this bill would have required the President to block property of any entity set up for or responsible for planning, building, or operating the Nord Stream 2 pipeline. It would also have required visa bans on corporate officers of those entities. The bill would have required the President to report to Congress before waiving certain Russia-related sanctions, and if Congress passed a joint resolution of disapproval, the President could not waive them.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that plan, build, or operate the Nord Stream 2 pipeline
who_it_affects.how: They would have faced required property-blocking sanctions, which would have frozen their U.S.-based assets and barred U.S. dealings with them.

who_it_affects.group: Corporate officers of Nord Stream 2 entities
who_it_affects.how: They would have faced required visa bans that would have blocked their entry into the United States.

who_it_affects.group: The President and executive branch agencies
who_it_affects.how: They would have been required to impose these sanctions and to report to Congress before waiving certain Russia-related sanctions.
They would have gained the ability to pass a joint resolution of disapproval that would have blocked a presidential waiver of certain Russia-related sanctions.
